+import time
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import httpx
+
+from polyfetch_scrape.response import Response
+from polyfetch_scrape.retry import RetryPolicy, should_retry
+
+
+class FetchError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a fetch fails after exhausting retries."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class _Attempt:
+    response: Response | None
+    retry_status: int | None
+    transport_error: Exception | None
+
+
+def fetch(
+    url: str,
+    *,
+    method: str = "GET",
+    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
+    timeout: float = 30.0,
+    retry: RetryPolicy | None = None,
+) -> Response:
+    policy = retry if retry is not None else RetryPolicy()
+    last = _Attempt(None, None, None)
+
+    with httpx.Client(timeout=timeout) as client:
+        for attempt_idx in range(policy.max_attempts):
+            last = _attempt_once(client, method, url, headers, policy)
+            if last.response is not None:
+                return last.response
+            if attempt_idx + 1 < policy.max_attempts:
+                time.sleep(policy.backoff_initial * (policy.backoff_factor**attempt_idx))
+
+    detail = (
+        f"status={last.retry_status}"
+        if last.retry_status is not None
+        else f"transport={last.transport_error!r}"
+    )
+    raise FetchError(
+        f"fetch failed after {policy.max_attempts} attempts ({detail}): {url}"
+    ) from last.transport_error
+
+
+def _attempt_once(
+    client: httpx.Client,
+    method: str,
+    url: str,
+    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None,
+    policy: RetryPolicy,
+) -> _Attempt:
+    try:
+        http_resp = client.request(method, url, headers=dict(headers) if headers else None)
+    except httpx.TransportError as exc:
+        return _Attempt(None, None, exc)
+
+    if should_retry(http_resp.status_code, policy):
+        return _Attempt(None, http_resp.status_code, None)
+
+    return _Attempt(_to_response(http_resp), None, None)
+
+
+def _to_response(http_resp: httpx.Response) -> Response:
+    return Response(
+        url=str(http_resp.url),
+        status=http_resp.status_code,
+        headers=dict(http_resp.headers),
+        body=http_resp.content,
+        content_type=http_resp.headers.get("content-type"),
+        backend="httpx",
+    )

feat: keyless local-leg run — run_local() + --local-only + make run_local (#133) (#137)

The documented run path (python -m doc_pipeline_engine.harness) ran run_both,
which fires the paid anthropic_sdk leg first and dies without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY,
so air-gapped / subscription users had no documented way to run the local leg.

--local-only CLI flag, and a make run_local target; run_both / DiffReport are
untouched. Document the run surface (env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL,
CLI switches) once in CONTRIBUTING, referenced from README, with the Makefile as
the command source of truth.

feat(stages): v2_normalize reconstructs heading tree (#33) (#43)

* feat(stages): v2_normalize reconstructs heading tree (#33)

Three regex families detect heading-like lines in Kreuzberg's flat
text — formal-prefix (SECTION/SEC./CHAPTER/ARTICLE/PART), numbered
with space (5.1 Title), numbered glued (1Title) — and split the body
at heading boundaries. Each detected heading becomes one section node
carrying title + body text; level is the numeric prefix dot-count
(capped at 6 per the schema). Falls back to single-leaf on zero
headings or density >50% of non-empty lines.

V2 now emits N claims per document instead of one. Five new tests
cover the three patterns plus both fallbacks; all gated on
is_valid("CanonicalDoc", …). v2_analyze / v2_render / v2_eval are
untouched per the plan's reuse principle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(prototype): add run-3 results for v2 heading tree

V2-only re-run on the five locked samples after #33. Legal goes
1 → 22 claims, spec 1 → 98, contract 1 → 13; invoice and diagram
correctly stay at 1 (no detectable headings). Updates the runs
index, adds a process.md bullet under "Normalization to
CanonicalDoc", and notes the change under [Unreleased] Changed in
CHANGELOG.

index d1505e0..76f1f37 100644

+++ b/src/doc_pipeline_engine/stages/v2_normalize.py
@@ -7,28 +7,96 @@
 #     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 """V2 normalize: ExtractionBundle → CanonicalDoc, deterministic.
 
-Kreuzberg's text is plain-text without layout structure, so the canonical
-tree is a single section containing the extracted text. tier_summary is a
-deterministic head-of-text excerpt — Quick tier (l0) takes the first 200
-chars, Comprehensive (l1) the first 1000.
+Kreuzberg returns plain text without layout structure, so we reconstruct a
+flat heading tree from heuristic detection over line prefixes (formal
+``SECTION``/``SEC.``/``CHAPTER``/``ARTICLE``/``PART``, numbered
+``5.1 Title``, glued numbered ``1Title``). Falls back to a single-leaf
+section when no headings or implausibly many headings are detected.
+tier_summary is a deterministic head-of-text excerpt — Quick (l0) takes
+the first 200 chars, Comprehensive (l1) the first 1000.
 """
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import re
 from datetime import datetime, timezone
 from typing import Any
 
 CONTRACT_VERSION = "0.1.0"
 _L0_CHARS = 200
 _L1_CHARS = 1000
+_HEADING_MAX_LEN = 100
+_DENSITY_CAP = 0.5
+_MAX_LEVEL = 6
+
+_FORMAL_PREFIX = re.compile(
+    r"^\s*(?P<kw>SECTION|SEC\.|CHAPTER|ARTICLE|PART)\s+\S+",
+)
+_NUM_SPACED = re.compile(r"^\s*(?P<num>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+\S")
+_NUM_GLUED = re.compile(r"^\s*(?P<num>\d+(?:\.\d+)*)(?P<rest>[A-Z]\S{3,}.*)$")
 
 
 def _truncate(text: str, n: int) -> str:
     return text if len(text) <= n else text[:n].rstrip() + "…"
 
 
+def _is_heading(line: str) -> tuple[bool, int, str]:
+    """Return (is_heading, level, title). level 0 means not a heading."""
+    stripped = line.strip()
+    if not stripped or len(stripped) > _HEADING_MAX_LEN:
+        return False, 0, ""
+    m = _FORMAL_PREFIX.match(stripped)
+    if m:
+        return True, 1, stripped
+    m = _NUM_SPACED.match(stripped)
+    if m:
+        level = min(m.group("num").count(".") + 1, _MAX_LEVEL)
+        return True, level, stripped
+    m = _NUM_GLUED.match(stripped)
+    if m:
+        level = min(m.group("num").count(".") + 1, _MAX_LEVEL)
+        return True, level, stripped
+    return False, 0, ""
+
+

+    stripped = line.strip()

+    m = _NUM_SPACED.match(stripped)
+    if m:

feat(v1): dispatch to claude CLI when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset (#30) (#41)

* feat(v1): dispatch to claude CLI when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset

Closes #30.

V1 stages already injected an optional Anthropic client via the
`client=` kwarg, with `make_client()` as the default. Without
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, `make_client()` (the Anthropic SDK constructor) just
crashes — that took the entire V1 leg of the prototype harness offline
in subscription-only codespaces.

Extend `_v1_client.call_text` / `call_json` with backend dispatch:

  explicit `client` → SDK with API key → `claude` CLI on PATH → raise

The CLI path shells out to `claude --print --output-format json
--system-prompt SYS --model M USER` and parses the `result` field from
the JSON envelope. Auth is the user's Claude subscription, so it works
anywhere `claude` is installed (already part of `make setup_dev`).
`is_error: true` envelopes raise. No new Python dep — `shutil.which`
checks for the binary at call time.

V1 stage signatures (`normalize_v1` / `analyze_v1` / `render_v1` /
`eval_v1`) are unchanged; existing stub-injection tests pass as-is.

Six new unit tests cover backend precedence, both happy paths, error
propagation, and the no-backend RuntimeError path. CI behavior is
unchanged: V1 stages stay outside the CI lane.

Verified locally with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset:
  call_text(None, model='claude-opus-4-7',
            system='Reply with the single word OK.', user='go')
  → 'OK'

* fix(v1): pass CLI user prompt via stdin to avoid argv E2BIG on long inputs

The contract DOCX sample (220K chars of extracted text) crashed the
claude CLI subprocess with `OSError: [Errno 7] Argument list too long`
because the user prompt was passed as a positional argv. Linux argv
limits hit around ~128K depending on env size.

Fix: pass the user prompt via subprocess stdin (`input=user`). System
prompt stays as a flag — it's always short and the CLI only accepts it
that way. Caught by the run-2 multi-sample E2E (legal/invoice/spec
samples were small enough to mask the bug; contract surfaced it).

Test updated: `captured["input"] == "hi"` asserted; `"hi" not in
captured["cmd"]` confirms the prompt no longer appears in argv.

feat(v1): dispatch to claude CLI when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset (#30) (#41)

* feat(v1): dispatch to claude CLI when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset

Closes #30.

V1 stages already injected an optional Anthropic client via the
`client=` kwarg, with `make_client()` as the default. Without
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, `make_client()` (the Anthropic SDK constructor) just
crashes — that took the entire V1 leg of the prototype harness offline
in subscription-only codespaces.

Extend `_v1_client.call_text` / `call_json` with backend dispatch:

  explicit `client` → SDK with API key → `claude` CLI on PATH → raise

The CLI path shells out to `claude --print --output-format json
--system-prompt SYS --model M USER` and parses the `result` field from
the JSON envelope. Auth is the user's Claude subscription, so it works
anywhere `claude` is installed (already part of `make setup_dev`).
`is_error: true` envelopes raise. No new Python dep — `shutil.which`
checks for the binary at call time.

V1 stage signatures (`normalize_v1` / `analyze_v1` / `render_v1` /
`eval_v1`) are unchanged; existing stub-injection tests pass as-is.

Six new unit tests cover backend precedence, both happy paths, error
propagation, and the no-backend RuntimeError path. CI behavior is
unchanged: V1 stages stay outside the CI lane.

Verified locally with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset:
  call_text(None, model='claude-opus-4-7',
            system='Reply with the single word OK.', user='go')
  → 'OK'

feat(v1): dispatch to claude CLI when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset (#30) (#41)

* feat(v1): dispatch to claude CLI when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset

Closes #30.

V1 stages already injected an optional Anthropic client via the
`client=` kwarg, with `make_client()` as the default. Without
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, `make_client()` (the Anthropic SDK constructor) just
crashes — that took the entire V1 leg of the prototype harness offline
in subscription-only codespaces.

Extend `_v1_client.call_text` / `call_json` with backend dispatch:

  explicit `client` → SDK with API key → `claude` CLI on PATH → raise

The CLI path shells out to `claude --print --output-format json
--system-prompt SYS --model M USER` and parses the `result` field from
the JSON envelope. Auth is the user's Claude subscription, so it works
anywhere `claude` is installed (already part of `make setup_dev`).
`is_error: true` envelopes raise. No new Python dep — `shutil.which`
checks for the binary at call time.

V1 stage signatures (`normalize_v1` / `analyze_v1` / `render_v1` /
`eval_v1`) are unchanged; existing stub-injection tests pass as-is.

Six new unit tests cover backend precedence, both happy paths, error
propagation, and the no-backend RuntimeError path. CI behavior is
unchanged: V1 stages stay outside the CI lane.

Verified locally with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset:
  call_text(None, model='claude-opus-4-7',
            system='Reply with the single word OK.', user='go')
  → 'OK'

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: note V1 backend dispatch in prototype/results, plan, README, CHANGELOG

Reflect the feat(v1) backend-dispatch change across the doc surface:

- prototype/results.md — close out the #30 follow-up bullet with
  resolution + cost-axis-honesty caveat (CLI mode reports
  total_cost_usd per call but doesn't yet stamp timings into
  EvalReport; treat CLI-vs-SDK latency comparisons as advisory).
- prototype/plan.md — add a one-paragraph note under Variant 1
  describing the backend dispatch order.
- README.md — quickstart note about ANTHROPIC_API_KEY OR claude CLI
  being acceptable for the V1 leg.
- CHANGELOG.md — Added (dispatch + tests) + Fixed (V1 leg now runs
  in subscription-only environments).

Architecture.md left alone — it doesn't mention V1 today; adding
backend-dispatch text there would be off-topic. Roadmap.md §0.2.0
similarly stays high-level.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(v1): pass CLI user prompt via stdin to avoid argv E2BIG on long inputs

The contract DOCX sample (220K chars of extracted text) crashed the
claude CLI subprocess with `OSError: [Errno 7] Argument list too long`
because the user prompt was passed as a positional argv. Linux argv
limits hit around ~128K depending on env size.

Fix: pass the user prompt via subprocess stdin (`input=user`). System
prompt stays as a flag — it's always short and the CLI only accepts it
that way. Caught by the run-2 multi-sample E2E (legal/invoice/spec
samples were small enough to mask the bug; contract surfaced it).

Test updated: `captured["input"] == "hi"` asserted; `"hi" not in
captured["cmd"]` confirms the prompt no longer appears in argv.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(results): per-run files under docs/prototype/results/, run-2 lands

Reshape: docs/prototype/results.md → docs/prototype/results/<dated>.md
so per-run snapshots accumulate without overwriting and trends are
easy to read.

- git mv results.md → results/2026-04-26-run-1-v2-only.md (PR #31's
  data, intra-doc links re-pointed to ../plan.md / ../samples.md)
- new results/2026-04-26-run-2-v1-cli.md — first fully-paired V1+V2
  run on all 5 samples; V1 dispatched via the claude CLI fallback.
  Per-sample axes (extract chars, V1/V2 wall times, latency ratio,
  md chars, claim counts), invoice content-delta example showing
  V1's 1.7K-char structured summary vs V2's 1-bullet trivial output,
  and faithfulness gaps (empty-OCR diagram honestly summarized;
  cost-axis honesty caveat).
- new results/README.md — index of runs + naming convention.
- samples.md "Run findings live in [results.md]" → [results/].
- CHANGELOG entries for the new docs + the stdin fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import io
+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class RenderArtifacts:
+    md: str
+    docx: bytes
+    pdf: bytes
+
+
+def _import_or_raise() -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
+    try:
+        import markdown as md_lib  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+        from docx import Document  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+        from weasyprint import HTML  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+    except ImportError as e:

+        ) from e

+    """Build a DOCX programmatically from Markdown.
+
+    Quick-tier scope only: headings (``#``..``######``) become Word headings,
+    everything else becomes a paragraph. Blank lines split blocks.
+    """
+    doc = document_cls()
+    doc.core_properties.title = title
+    for block in md_source.split("\n\n"):
+        block = block.strip()
+        if not block:

+        if match:
+            level = len(match.group(1))
+            doc.add_heading(match.group(2).strip(), level=level)
+        else:
+            doc.add_paragraph(block)
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    doc.save(buf)
+    return buf.getvalue()
+

+    html = md_lib.markdown(md_source)
+    return html_cls(string=html).write_pdf()

feat(render): shared Markdown → DOCX + PDF render utility (#19)

* feat(render): add Markdown → DOCX + PDF render utility

Shared converter used by both V1 (Claude-written Markdown) and V2
(Jinja-rendered Markdown). Keeping conversion deterministic and shared
means the V1-vs-V2 A/B is purely about Markdown content, not about
the rendering path.

Public API:
  RenderArtifacts        dataclass: md (str), docx (bytes), pdf (bytes)
  render_artifacts(md, title) -> RenderArtifacts

Imports of markdown / python-docx / weasyprint are deferred so the
module loads without the optional render extra; calling render_artifacts
without it raises a clear hint to run uv sync --extra render.

DOCX is built programmatically: # heading lines become Word headings via
add_heading(level=N); other blocks become paragraphs via add_paragraph.
Quick-tier scope only — no full Markdown→DOCX semantic mapping; we add
list/table support later if Comprehensive tier needs it.

PDF goes Markdown → HTML (markdown lib) → PDF (WeasyPrint, pure-Python).
No GPL, no JVM, no Pandoc.

Tests use pytest.importorskip to gate on the optional libraries so CI
without the render extra still passes.

+# Copyright 2026 qte77

+"""Markdown → DOCX + PDF conversion.
+
+Imports for ``markdown``, ``docx``, and ``weasyprint`` are deferred so this
+module loads without the ``render`` extra. Calling ``render_artifacts``
+without the extra raises a clear hint to install it.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import io
+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class RenderArtifacts:
+    md: str
+    docx: bytes
+    pdf: bytes
+
+
+def _import_or_raise() -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
+    try:
+        import markdown as md_lib  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+        from docx import Document  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+        from weasyprint import HTML  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
+    except ImportError as e:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "Render extras not installed. Install with: uv sync --extra render"
+        ) from e
+    return md_lib, Document, HTML
+
+
+def _markdown_to_docx_bytes(md_source: str, title: str, document_cls: Any) -> bytes:
+    """Build a DOCX programmatically from Markdown.
+
+    Quick-tier scope only: headings (``#``..``######``) become Word headings,
+    everything else becomes a paragraph. Blank lines split blocks.
+    """
+    doc = document_cls()
+    doc.core_properties.title = title
+    for block in md_source.split("\n\n"):
+        block = block.strip()
+        if not block:
+            continue
+        match = _HEADING_RE.match(block)
+        if match:
+            level = len(match.group(1))
+            doc.add_heading(match.group(2).strip(), level=level)
+        else:
+            doc.add_paragraph(block)
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    doc.save(buf)
+    return buf.getvalue()
+
+
+def _markdown_to_pdf_bytes(md_source: str, md_lib: Any, html_cls: Any) -> bytes:
+    html = md_lib.markdown(md_source)
+    return html_cls(string=html).write_pdf()
+
+
+def render_artifacts(markdown_source: str, title: str) -> RenderArtifacts:
+    """Convert Markdown to DOCX (python-docx) and PDF (markdown→html→WeasyPrint).
+
+    The Markdown source is returned unchanged; DOCX and PDF are byte payloads.
+    Deterministic for a given library version set.
+    """
+    md_lib, document_cls, html_cls = _import_or_raise()
+    return RenderArtifacts(
+        md=markdown_source,
+        docx=_markdown_to_docx_bytes(markdown_source, title, document_cls),
+        pdf=_markdown_to_pdf_bytes(markdown_source, md_lib, html_cls),
+    )

feat(stages): add discover and Kreuzberg extract stages (#18)

* feat(stages): add discover stage (filesystem → DiscoveryManifest)

Pure-stdlib stage: walks ``root`` with the given glob, computes sha256
per file, and emits a DiscoveryManifest dict ready for gate validation.
Sorted output for deterministic re-runs.

Public API:
  discover(root: Path, glob: str = "**/*") -> dict

Tests (TDD per python-dev / tdd-core):
  test_stages_discover_emits_valid_discovery_manifest
  test_stages_discover_lists_files_with_sha256_and_size
  test_stages_discover_respects_glob_filter
  test_stages_discover_source_records_root_and_kind

This is the first half of plan PR 2; extract stage lands in the next
commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(stages): add Kreuzberg-backed extract adapter

Kreuzberg is a single Python-native, MIT-licensed extractor covering
PDF, Office, images (via Tesseract), email, and text — chosen as the
shared extraction stage in the prototype plan to eliminate extraction
as an A/B confound between V1 and V2.

The kreuzberg import is deferred so the module loads without the extra
installed; calling extract() without the extra raises a clear hint to
run uv sync --extra extract. Unit tests substitute the kreuzberg call
via monkeypatch and run without the extra in CI.

Public API:
  extract(file_entry: dict, source_root: Path) -> dict   # ExtractionBundle

Adapter identity: name="kreuzberg", version=kreuzberg.__version__.

pyproject.toml gains [project.optional-dependencies] extract extra =
"kreuzberg>=2.0". CHANGELOG records the runtime additions from PRs
#16, #17, and this PR under [Unreleased].

Plain-text "§0.2.0 runner scaffold" → linked to
[§0.2.0 — Runner](docs/roadmap.md#020--runner) so readers can navigate
to the roadmap entry the scaffold implements.

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+# Copyright 2026 qte77
+#
+# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+# You may obtain a copy of the License at
+#
+#     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+"""Discover stage: filesystem walk → DiscoveryManifest.
+
+Walks ``root`` with the given glob, computes sha256 per file, and emits a
+DiscoveryManifest dict ready for gate validation.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+CONTRACT_VERSION = "0.1.0"
+_HASH_CHUNK = 65536
+
+
+def _sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as f:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(_HASH_CHUNK), b""):
+            h.update(chunk)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def discover(root: Path, glob: str = "**/*") -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Walk ``root`` matching ``glob``, return a DiscoveryManifest dict."""
+    files: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for path in sorted(root.glob(glob)):
+        if not path.is_file():
+            continue
+        files.append(
+            {
+                "path": str(path.relative_to(root)),
+                "size_bytes": path.stat().st_size,
+                "sha256": _sha256(path),
+                "file_type": path.suffix.lstrip(".").lower() or "bin",
+            }
+        )
+    return {
+        "version": CONTRACT_VERSION,
+        "source": {"root": str(root), "kind": "folder"},
+        "discovered_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+        "files": files,
+    }

+        "discovered_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+        "files": files,

feat(stages): add discover and Kreuzberg extract stages (#18)

* feat(stages): add discover stage (filesystem → DiscoveryManifest)

Pure-stdlib stage: walks ``root`` with the given glob, computes sha256
per file, and emits a DiscoveryManifest dict ready for gate validation.
Sorted output for deterministic re-runs.

Public API:
  discover(root: Path, glob: str = "**/*") -> dict

Tests (TDD per python-dev / tdd-core):
  test_stages_discover_emits_valid_discovery_manifest
  test_stages_discover_lists_files_with_sha256_and_size
  test_stages_discover_respects_glob_filter
  test_stages_discover_source_records_root_and_kind

This is the first half of plan PR 2; extract stage lands in the next
commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(stages): add Kreuzberg-backed extract adapter

Kreuzberg is a single Python-native, MIT-licensed extractor covering
PDF, Office, images (via Tesseract), email, and text — chosen as the
shared extraction stage in the prototype plan to eliminate extraction
as an A/B confound between V1 and V2.

The kreuzberg import is deferred so the module loads without the extra
installed; calling extract() without the extra raises a clear hint to
run uv sync --extra extract. Unit tests substitute the kreuzberg call
via monkeypatch and run without the extra in CI.

Public API:
  extract(file_entry: dict, source_root: Path) -> dict   # ExtractionBundle

Adapter identity: name="kreuzberg", version=kreuzberg.__version__.

pyproject.toml gains [project.optional-dependencies] extract extra =
"kreuzberg>=2.0". CHANGELOG records the runtime additions from PRs
#16, #17, and this PR under [Unreleased].

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: hyperlink §0.2.0 reference in CHANGELOG

Plain-text "§0.2.0 runner scaffold" → linked to
[§0.2.0 — Runner](docs/roadmap.md#020--runner) so readers can navigate
to the roadmap entry the scaffold implements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(runner): add stage-chain runner with gate validation (§0.2.0) (#16)

Implements the minimum viable pipeline: a stage chain that threads each
stage's output dict into the next, validating against its declared
contract via base.contracts.validate. Halts on first failure with a
PipelineError carrying stage_name, contract_name, and the underlying

+# Copyright 2026 qte77

+# You may obtain a copy of the License at
+#

+"""Runner chain behavior: passes valid outputs through, halts on first
+gate failure, and surfaces stage and contract names in the error.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+import pytest
+
+from doc_pipeline_engine.runner import PipelineError, run
+
+SHA_ZERO = "0" * 64
+NOW = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
+
+
+def _valid_discovery_manifest(_seed: dict) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "version": "0.1.0",
+        "source": {"root": "/data/ingest", "kind": "folder"},
+        "discovered_at": NOW,
+        "files": [
+            {
+                "path": "a.pdf",
+                "size_bytes": 100,
+                "sha256": SHA_ZERO,
+                "file_type": "pdf",
+            }
+        ],
+    }
+
+
+def _valid_extraction_bundle(_manifest: dict) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "version": "0.1.0",
+        "source_path": "a.pdf",
+        "source_sha256": SHA_ZERO,
+        "adapter": {"name": "stub", "version": "0.0.0"},
+        "extracted_at": NOW,
+        "content": {"text": "hi", "layout": []},
+    }
+
+
+def _invalid_extraction_bundle(_manifest: dict) -> dict:
+    bundle = _valid_extraction_bundle(_manifest)
+    del bundle["content"]
+    return bundle
+
+

+    stages = [
+        ("discover", _valid_discovery_manifest, "DiscoveryManifest"),
+        ("extract", _valid_extraction_bundle, "ExtractionBundle"),
+    ]
+
+    outputs = run(stages, seed={})
+
+    assert len(outputs) == 2
+    assert outputs[0]["files"][0]["path"] == "a.pdf"
+    assert outputs[1]["adapter"]["name"] == "stub"
+
+
+def test_runner_chain_halts_on_first_invalid_output() -> None:
+    stages = [
+        ("discover", _valid_discovery_manifest, "DiscoveryManifest"),
+        ("extract", _invalid_extraction_bundle, "ExtractionBundle"),
+    ]
+
+    with pytest.raises(PipelineError):
+        run(stages, seed={})
+
+
+def test_runner_pipeline_error_contains_stage_and_contract_names() -> None:
+    stages = [
+        ("discover", _valid_discovery_manifest, "DiscoveryManifest"),
+        ("extract", _invalid_extraction_bundle, "ExtractionBundle"),
+    ]
+
+    with pytest.raises(PipelineError) as exc:
+        run(stages, seed={})
+
+    assert exc.value.stage_name == "extract"
+    assert exc.value.contract_name == "ExtractionBundle"
+    assert "extract" in str(exc.value)
+    assert "ExtractionBundle" in str(exc.value)

feat(runner): add stage-chain runner with gate validation (§0.2.0) (#16)

Implements the minimum viable pipeline: a stage chain that threads each
stage's output dict into the next, validating against its declared
contract via base.contracts.validate. Halts on first failure with a
PipelineError carrying stage_name, contract_name, and the underlying
jsonschema detail.

Public API:

  base.adapter.AdapterBase   abstract base for extraction backends
                             (extract: file_entry -> ExtractionBundle)
  runner.Stage               (stage_name, callable, output_contract_name)
  runner.PipelineError       raised on first gate failure
  runner.run(stages, seed)   threads outputs; returns list of stage results

Tests (TDD, RED-GREEN-REFACTOR per python-dev / tdd-core):
  test_runner_chain_passes_valid_outputs_through_all_stages
  test_runner_chain_halts_on_first_invalid_output
  test_runner_pipeline_error_contains_stage_and_contract_names

Stages dir created as empty __init__.py; concrete stages land per phase
in subsequent PRs (discover/extract in PR 2; render/formats in PR 3;
v1_* in PR 4; v2_* in PR 5).

Refs: docs/roadmap.md §0.2.0, docs/prototype-plan.md, plan file
docs-pipeline-prototype-plan.md.

+# Copyright 2026 qte77

+# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+# You may obtain a copy of the License at
+#
+#     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+"""Stage chain runner with gate validation.
+
+A stage is a 3-tuple ``(name, callable, output_contract_name)``. The runner
+threads the output of each stage into the next, validating the output
+against its declared contract via `base.contracts.validate`. The chain
+halts on the first validation failure with a `PipelineError` carrying the
+offending stage name and contract.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import Any
+
+import jsonschema
+
+from doc_pipeline_engine.base.contracts import validate
+
+StageCallable = Callable[[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any]]
+Stage = tuple[str, StageCallable, str]
+
+
+class PipelineError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a stage output fails its contract gate."""
+
+    def __init__(self, stage_name: str, contract_name: str, detail: str) -> None:
+        self.stage_name = stage_name
+        self.contract_name = contract_name
+        self.detail = detail
+        super().__init__(
+            f"stage={stage_name!r} contract={contract_name!r}: {detail}"
+        )
+
+
+def run(stages: list[Stage], seed: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Execute stages in order, validating each output against its contract."""
+    outputs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    current: dict[str, Any] = seed
+    for stage_name, fn, contract_name in stages:
+        result = fn(current)
+        try:
+            validate(contract_name, result)
+        except jsonschema.ValidationError as e:
+            raise PipelineError(stage_name, contract_name, e.message) from e
+        outputs.append(result)
+        current = result
+    return outputs

+"""Runner chain behavior: passes valid outputs through, halts on first
+gate failure, and surfaces stage and contract names in the error.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+import pytest
+
+from doc_pipeline_engine.runner import PipelineError, run
+
+SHA_ZERO = "0" * 64
+NOW = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
+
+
+def _valid_discovery_manifest(_seed: dict) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "version": "0.1.0",
+        "source": {"root": "/data/ingest", "kind": "folder"},
+        "discovered_at": NOW,
+        "files": [
+            {
+                "path": "a.pdf",
+                "size_bytes": 100,
+                "sha256": SHA_ZERO,
+                "file_type": "pdf",
+            }
+        ],
+    }
+
+
+def _valid_extraction_bundle(_manifest: dict) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "version": "0.1.0",
+        "source_path": "a.pdf",
+        "source_sha256": SHA_ZERO,
+        "adapter": {"name": "stub", "version": "0.0.0"},
+        "extracted_at": NOW,
+        "content": {"text": "hi", "layout": []},
+    }
+
+
+def _invalid_extraction_bundle(_manifest: dict) -> dict:
+    bundle = _valid_extraction_bundle(_manifest)
+    del bundle["content"]
+    return bundle
+
+
+def test_runner_chain_passes_valid_outputs_through_all_stages() -> None:
+    stages = [
+        ("discover", _valid_discovery_manifest, "DiscoveryManifest"),
+        ("extract", _valid_extraction_bundle, "ExtractionBundle"),
+    ]
+
+    outputs = run(stages, seed={})
+
+    assert len(outputs) == 2
+    assert outputs[0]["files"][0]["path"] == "a.pdf"
+    assert outputs[1]["adapter"]["name"] == "stub"
+
+
+def test_runner_chain_halts_on_first_invalid_output() -> None:
+    stages = [
+        ("discover", _valid_discovery_manifest, "DiscoveryManifest"),
+        ("extract", _invalid_extraction_bundle, "ExtractionBundle"),
+    ]
+
+    with pytest.raises(PipelineError):
+        run(stages, seed={})
+
+
+def test_runner_pipeline_error_contains_stage_and_contract_names() -> None:
+    stages = [
+        ("discover", _valid_discovery_manifest, "DiscoveryManifest"),
+        ("extract", _invalid_extraction_bundle, "ExtractionBundle"),
+    ]
+
+    with pytest.raises(PipelineError) as exc:
+        run(stages, seed={})
+
+    assert exc.value.stage_name == "extract"
+    assert exc.value.contract_name == "ExtractionBundle"
+    assert "extract" in str(exc.value)
+    assert "ExtractionBundle" in str(exc.value)
